title: Müller wins a wet, red-flagged finale to seal second in the standings
dek: Nico Müller won the rain-hit DTM finale at Hockenheim from pole, 3.835 seconds clear of Mike Rockenfeller, in a 27-lap race interrupted by a red flag after an Aston Martin caught fire.

chapters.title: Rast's win and Müller's costly Saturday
text: Saturday had gone to René Rast, who beat Marco Wittmann by 1.693 seconds after a safety car cancelled the BMW's undercut, and whose win handed Audi Sport Team Rosberg the teams' title. For Nico Müller, the fight for second place in the drivers' standings with Wittmann had been damaged on Saturday: he took a stop under the safety car, which did not count as his mandatory one, and a drive-through for speeding in the pit lane left him 17th.

Mike Rockenfeller had finished third, but he collected a third warning on Saturday, which carried a five-place grid penalty into Sunday. Jenson Button's ninth had been the best result by a Super GT guest. Rain was forecast for the finale, which the Japanese drivers expected to be harder still.

chapters.title: Rockenfeller's pole is taken away
text: Qualifying took place in torrential rain. Müller came out on top of the early battle and strung together two quicker laps in the final five minutes for a 1m50.813s, which looked like the benchmark. Rockenfeller then improved by 0.013 seconds to 1m50.800s, but the third warning triggered the five-place penalty, and Müller inherited pole position.

Timo Glock, third fastest in the best-placed BMW, moved up alongside Müller on the front row, with Jamie Green and Joel Eriksson behind them, Wittmann fifth and Rockenfeller dropping to sixth. Philipp Eng was seventh and Rast, who said his session had been untidy and full of traffic, eighth. Robin Frijns, Loïc Duval and Jake Dennis, the leading Aston Martin, completed the top eleven.

Cassidy was the quickest Super GT driver, 1.727 seconds off pole, with Button and Ronnie Quintarelli further back. Pietro Fittipaldi was sent to the back of the grid, and BMW asked for the seal on an additional engine to be opened, which meant its first four cars in the race would not count for the manufacturers' championship.

chapters.title: A fire, a crash and a long stop before the race really begins
text: Paul di Resta's Aston Martin stopped on the formation lap and never started. Müller then got away cleanly at the standing start, while Rast shot from eighth to second within the first corners. Rockenfeller, Glock and Wittmann joined the fight for the places behind him.

It ended almost at once. Cassidy, racing alongside Aberdein's WRT Audi, touched the Audi and spun into the wall at the Mercedes-Arena. The safety car came out, and then Daniel Juncadella's Aston Martin pulled off and began to burn. Juncadella got out of the car, the race was red-flagged and the field waited for the fire to be put out. The stoppage lasted some ten to thirteen minutes, and the race restarted behind the safety car. Only 27 laps were completed, in 1h04m45s.

Before the restart Eng and Fittipaldi were each given a drive-through penalty for breaking the three-minute rule, which requires the cars to be off their jacks with the tyres fitted three minutes before the start.

chapters.title: Müller covers Rast, Wittmann's release ends his podium hopes
text: The mandatory stops began early. Button was first in on lap four, Quintarelli stopped straight after the restart, and on lap five most of the leading group came in together, including Rockenfeller, Wittmann, Glock and Frijns. Wittmann, who had run fourth, was released into the path of Aberdein's Audi and touched it; the stewards called it an unsafe release and gave him a drive-through that left him twelfth at the flag.

Quintarelli's stop did not count as his mandatory one, because it was made straight after the safety car had gone in, and he had to come in again later. Button, whose stop had cost him badly on Saturday, took 8.8 seconds this time.

Müller pitted on lap six of 27, and Rast followed a lap later with the quicker stop to emerge ahead. Rast then struggled for grip on his second set of tyres; he ran wide at Turn 10, and Müller took the lead back. Rockenfeller passed his fellow Audi driver soon afterwards, and Rast could not hold the pace on the wet track.

chapters.title: Green and Eriksson gamble, Müller wins by 3.8 seconds
text: Müller was clear but the winner was not certain until the last lap, because Green and Eriksson had stayed out on their first set of tyres. Green led the second stint for long stretches before both men finally came in on the penultimate lap. Green rejoined fourth, just ahead of Glock, but on cold tyres he could not stay in front of the BMW, and Glock finished fourth, about three and a half seconds from the podium. Green was fifth and Eriksson sixth.

Müller took the flag 3.835 seconds ahead of Rockenfeller, who had worked his way from sixth on the grid to second, with Rast completing an Audi sweep of the podium 8.403 seconds back. Frijns was seventh, Dennis eighth as the best Aston Martin, Bruno Spengler ninth and Duval tenth. Ferdinand Habsburg was 11th, Wittmann 12th and Sheldon van der Linde 13th.

Button was 16th, Quintarelli 17th and a lap down, and Aberdein, who had been involved in contact with both Cassidy and Wittmann, retired on lap 14. Rockenfeller set the fastest lap, a 1m52.014s on lap 22.

chapters.title: Second place secured and a record Audi season
text: Müller's third win of the season secured second place in the championship ahead of Wittmann, a result he called a good way to finish after the setbacks of Saturday's safety car. Rast ended the year as champion on 322 points, Müller second on 250 and Wittmann third on 202. Wittmann had been in contention for the podium until his unsafe release, and BMW's motorsport director Jens Marquardt called the weekend a difficult end to a difficult season, and said the team had made things harder for itself with its penalties.

For Audi it was the most successful DTM season in its history. The RS 5 DTM took twelve wins, with Audi filling the top three places in the teams' standings through Rosberg, Abt and Phoenix, and it also took the manufacturers' title. All six Audi works drivers scored in the finale.

R-Motorsport's first DTM season ended with a fire and a car that never started. Team principal Florian Kamelger said he was proud of the season and that the second year would be one of consolidation. WRT's Vincent Vosse said his team was pleased with the progress of its customer Audis, and both teams were committed to 2020.

The guests from Super GT went home with some lessons. Button said the Super GT teams could not get the wet tyres into their working window and that the cars were running about three seconds slower than the DTM cars. The two series will meet again at Fuji in November for the Dream Race, in which Audi will field Rast, Rockenfeller, Duval and Benoit Treluyer and BMW will run Alex Zanardi, Kamui Kobayashi and Wittmann.

facts.t: Red flag for a burning Aston Martin
facts.v: Juncadella's Aston Martin caught fire on the first lap and the race was stopped for about 13 minutes, so only 27 laps were run.
